items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: a friend of his named Joe Sherman that owned the Sherman Bar

ctx.x: I’m going to tell you about that deal. When I was looking for a girl singer, and I got to Chicago, the band had been popular, but the band was always popular because I was popular, and I could carry the band myself because I was the first black musician to play in a white band. See and Teddy Wilson was playing with Benny, but he used to play

when Benny used to take intermission, and no white musicians was on stage, then Teddy would play, by himself see? So I was the first one, legally to break that tradition down. But you know the funny thing about it, there wasn’t no black and white playing together no place. Not in pictures, moving pictures, not in baseball, or football, no kind of sports. The Benny Goodman quartet was the first mixed group and it was, you know? So I was playing in Chicago at the Regal Theater, that’s the black theater on the south…
